questions.question: Which description defines an open queueing network of $M$ stations, with external arrival rates $\gamma_i$ and routing probabilities $P_{ij}$ from station $i$ to station $j$?
options: Every station receives new jobs from outside, so $\gamma_i>0$ for each $i$, and every job eventually leaves.
New jobs enter at rates $\gamma_i$, and no job ever returns to a station that it has already visited.
New jobs arrive at rates $\gamma_i\geq0$ with $\sum_i\gamma_i>0$, and every job eventually leaves the network.
Each row of the routing matrix sums to one, so after every service a job moves on to another station.

questions.question: In an open network, jobs visit stations 1, 2, 3 in that order; all new jobs arrive at station 1 at rate $\gamma_1>0$, and after station 3 a job returns to station 1 with probability $p$ or leaves. If $p$ rises from 0.1 to 0.2 and the network stays stable, what happens to the network's exit rate and to $\lambda_1$?
options: The exit rate of the network stays $\gamma_1$, while the arrival rate $\lambda_1$ at station 1 increases.
Both the exit rate of the network and the arrival rate $\lambda_1$ at station 1 increase.
Neither changes, because station arrival rates are fixed by the external rate $\gamma_1$.
The exit rate of the network falls below $\gamma_1$, while the arrival rate $\lambda_1$ increases.

questions.question: Which three assumptions turn an open queueing network with single-server stations into a Jackson network, in which each station behaves as an $M/M/1$ queue?
options: Poisson external arrivals, general service-time distributions, and Markov routing independent of everything else.
Poisson external arrivals, exponential service times, and Markov routing independent of everything else.
External arrivals with any interarrival-time distribution, exponential service times, and Markov routing.
Poisson external arrivals, exponential service times, and no feedback, so that no station is visited twice.

questions.question: In an open network with external rates $\gamma_i$ and routing probabilities $P_{ij}$ from station $i$ to station $j$, which equation gives the total arrival rate $\lambda_i$ at station $i$ when every station is rate stable?
options: $\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j=1}^M\lambda_jP_{ij}$
$\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j=1}^M\gamma_jP_{ji}$
$\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j=1}^M\lambda_jP_{ji}-\lambda_iP_{i0}$
$\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j=1}^M\lambda_jP_{ji}$

questions.question: In a stable open network, station $i$ has arrival rate $\lambda_i$ and mean sojourn time per visit $\mathbb{E}[J_i]$, and $L_i$ is the number of jobs at station $i$. What does the product $\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[J_i]$ equal?
options: The mean total time that one job spends at station $i$, summed over all its visits to that station.
The load $\rho_i$ of station $i$, that is, the long-run fraction of time that its server is busy.
The mean number of jobs $\mathbb{E}[L_i]$ at station $i$, counting both waiting jobs and the job in service.
The mean number of jobs in the whole network, since every job that visits station $i$ is counted there.

questions.question: In an open network, new jobs arrive at station 1 at rate $\gamma_1=5$ and at station 2 at rate $\gamma_2=2$ per hour. After station 1 a job goes to station 2 with probability 0.4 and leaves otherwise; after station 2 every job leaves. What is the arrival rate $\lambda_2$ at station 2?
options: $\lambda_2=7$ per hour
$\lambda_2=4$ per hour
$\lambda_2=2$ per hour
$\lambda_2=5$ per hour

questions.question: A stable open network has external rates $\boldsymbol{\gamma}=(2,0.5,0)$ per hour, station arrival rates $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=(2.5,3,2.5)$ per hour and mean numbers of jobs $(\mathbb{E}[L_1],\mathbb{E}[L_2],\mathbb{E}[L_3])=(2,3,1.5)$. What is the mean total sojourn time $\mathbb{E}[J]$ of a job in the network?
options: $\mathbb{E}[J]=0.8125$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=16.25$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=3.25$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=2.6$ hours

questions.question: In an open network, after station 1 a job goes to station 2 w.p. 0.6, to station 3 w.p. 0.3 and leaves otherwise; after station 2 it goes to station 3 w.p. 0.5 and leaves otherwise; after station 3 it returns to station 1 w.p. 0.25 and leaves otherwise. With $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=(2.5,2.5,2)$ per hour, at what rate do jobs leave the network from station 3?
options: $1.5$ jobs per hour
$2$ jobs per hour
$0.5$ jobs per hour
$0.4$ jobs per hour

questions.question: A stable open Jackson network has two single-server stations with station arrival rates $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=(2.5,3)$ per hour and mean service times $(\mathbb{E}[S_1],\mathbb{E}[S_2])=(0.2,0.25)$ hours. What is the mean number of jobs $\mathbb{E}[L]$ in the network, counting jobs in service?
options: $\mathbb{E}[L]=6$
$\mathbb{E}[L]=1.25$
$\mathbb{E}[L]=4$
$\mathbb{E}[L]=3$

questions.question: A stable open network has external rates $\gamma_1=2$ and $\gamma_2=1$ per hour, and the traffic equations give station arrival rates $\lambda_1=3.5$ and $\lambda_2=4.5$ per hour. What is the expected number of visits that a job makes to station 2?
options: $4.5$ visits
$1.5$ visits
$0.5625$ visits
$2.25$ visits

questions.question: In an open network, new jobs arrive only at station 1, at rate $\gamma_1>0$. After station 1 every job goes to station 2, after station 2 every job goes to station 3, and after station 3 every job returns to station 2. What can be said about this network?
options: It is stable once the servers at stations 2 and 3 are fast enough, since faster service clears the cycle sooner.
Stations 2 and 3 form a closed network with a fixed population, so the network as a whole is stable.
Only station 1 matters for stability, since it is the only station that receives jobs from outside.
The traffic equations have no solution; jobs pile up at stations 2 and 3 whatever their service speeds.

questions.question: A stable open network has Poisson external arrivals and Markov routing, but general (not exponential) service times at its single-server stations. Which pair of results is guaranteed to hold for every such network, whatever its routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$?
options: The traffic equations $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=\boldsymbol{\gamma}+\boldsymbol{\lambda}\boldsymbol{P}$ and the network relation $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|\,\mathbb{E}[J]=\mathbb{E}[L]$
The traffic equations $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=\boldsymbol{\gamma}+\boldsymbol{\lambda}\boldsymbol{P}$ and the product form of the joint distribution of the $L_i$
The network relation $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|\,\mathbb{E}[J]=\mathbb{E}[L]$ and Poisson arrival streams at every station
The traffic equations $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=\boldsymbol{\gamma}+\boldsymbol{\lambda}\boldsymbol{P}$ and the relation $\bigl(\sum_i\lambda_i\bigr)\mathbb{E}[J]=\mathbb{E}[L]$

questions.question: In a Jackson network without feedback, every station is a stable single-server station with exponential service. Why is the arrival stream at each downstream station a Poisson process?
options: Exponential service makes each station release jobs as a Poisson process with rate $1/\mathbb{E}[S_i]$.
Markov routing turns any stream that it splits into Poisson streams, whatever the interarrival times.
A stationary $M/M/1$ queue's departures are Poisson with rate $\lambda$, and splitting and merging keep streams Poisson.
Little's law gives each station equal arrival and departure rates, which forces both streams to be Poisson.

questions.question: Jobs arrive as a Poisson process at rate $\lambda=3$ per hour and visit two exponential single-server stations in tandem, once each, with $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=0.2$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=0.25$ hours. What is the mean sojourn time $\mathbb{E}[J]$ of a job in the line?
options: $\mathbb{E}[J]=0.45$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=1.5$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=1.05$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=4.5$ hours

questions.question: In a Jackson network, new jobs arrive only at station 1, at rate $\gamma_1=3$ per hour. After station 1 every job goes to station 2; after station 2 a job returns to station 1 w.p. 0.25 and leaves otherwise. Station 1 has one exponential server with $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=0.25$ hours. Which statement about its load $\rho_1$ is correct?
options: $\lambda_1=2.25$ gives $\rho_1=0.5625$, below one, so station 1 is stable.
Returned jobs raise $\lambda_1$ to $3.75$, so $\rho_1=0.9375$ and station 1 is stable.
$\rho_1=1$ exactly, and a load equal to one still keeps station 1 stable.
$\rho_1=1$, so the strict condition $\rho_1<1$ fails and station 1 is unstable.

questions.question: In a stable open network, new jobs arrive at station 1 at rate 4 and at station 2 at rate 1 per hour. After station 1 a job goes to station 2 w.p. 0.25 and leaves otherwise; after station 2 every job leaves. The mean sojourn times per visit are $\mathbb{E}[J_1]=0.5$ and $\mathbb{E}[J_2]=2$ hours. What is $\mathbb{E}[J]$ for an arbitrary job?
options: $\mathbb{E}[J]=1.2$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=2.5$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=1$ hour
$\mathbb{E}[J]=1.25$ hours

questions.question: An open network has external rates $\gamma_i$ and single-server stations with mean service times $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$; stability requires $\rho_i=\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]<1$ at every station. How does the condition $\gamma_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]<1$ for every station $i$ relate to stability?
options: It guarantees stability, but some stable networks violate it.
It holds exactly when the network is stable.
Every stable network satisfies it, but it does not guarantee stability.
Stability neither implies it nor follows from it.

questions.question: In a Jackson network, a job may return to single-server station 1 after visiting station 3, and $\rho_i<1$ at every station. A student argues that the arrival stream at station 1 need not be Poisson, so $\mathbb{E}[J_1]=\mathbb{E}[S_1]/(1-\rho_1)$ cannot be used. Which assessment is correct?
options: The student is right: with feedback this formula fails, and only simulation gives $\mathbb{E}[J_1]$.
The formula is only an approximation here, like the tandem-line approximations for general service.
The formula holds and gives the total time that a job spends at station 1 over all its visits.
The formula holds with $\rho_1=\lambda_1\mathbb{E}[S_1]$ and gives the mean sojourn time per visit.

questions.question: In a Jackson network with one single-server station, new jobs arrive at rate $\gamma=2$ per hour and $\mathbb{E}[S]=0.3$ hours. After each service a job is sent back for rework with probability 0.2 and leaves otherwise. What is the mean total sojourn time $\mathbb{E}[J]$ of a job?
options: $\mathbb{E}[J]=1.5$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=1.2$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=0.9375$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=1.44$ hours

questions.question: In an open Jackson network, all new jobs arrive at station 1 at rate $\gamma$. After station 1 a job goes to station 2 or 3 w.p. 0.5 each; after station 2 it goes to station 3; after station 3 it returns to station 1 w.p. 0.25 and leaves otherwise. With single servers and $(\mathbb{E}[S_1],\mathbb{E}[S_2],\mathbb{E}[S_3])=(0.1,0.3,0.12)$ hours, for which $\gamma$ is the network stable?
options: For $\gamma<\tfrac{10}{3}$ per hour
For $\gamma<5$ per hour
For $\gamma<7.5$ per hour
For $\gamma<\tfrac{20}{3}$ per hour
